newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Shell restarting all Nigeria oil operations Monday.
newsitem.headline: Shell restarting all Nigeria oil operations Monday.

text.p: The Nigerian unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group said on Monday it was restarting oil output at all locations in the Niger delta following the restoration of peace after last week's community disturbances.
"We intend to restart production today at Egwa, Jones Creek and Odidi areas," a company spokesman in Lagos said, referring to flow stations which contribute to Shell's Forcados export stream.

He said output had started at all five oil flow stations in the Bonny export system's Nembe creek in the southeast, which were also shut down on March 22 by a political dispute between villagers and the military government.

"Nembe production is back to normal. Three flow stations had restarted by Saturday, two yesterday and by midday production was back to normal," he said, adding that, "Except for minor problems like terminal capacity the situation is now all right."
Earlier on Monday a Shell official said production on Monday still was running some 160,000 barrels a day (bpd) below normal at 790,000 bpd.
Shell has declared force majeure on four cargoes of early April loading Forcados, delaying the shipments by three days. No export shipments have yet been cancelled.

Militant villagers protesting against a merger of two communities and relocation of the capital of another council area last week disrupted Shell's operations in both the west and the east of the Niger delta, shutting in a total of 210,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil.
The Shell spokesman said peace had been fully restored in the oil producing areas and the last of the Shell oil workers held hostage were released on Thursday.
Nigerian oil communities have long been restive over the lack of modern amenities in their vicinities and frequently vent their anger by disrupting oil production activities.
